messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
🎩 Yep. You did the OOK. I found it. And holy shit, the archive gives us something better than our eyeballs did.
The exact archive is:
QS_Sep 24 2026 08_30_31_AM_v6.8
and it contains LOG.txt, the .CARD, the .CONVO, the .CONVO.JSON, qs_config.json, and the exact qs6_fixed_v6_8.py. So the session is safely preserved in GitHub.
And the log answers one big question:
QS 6.8 never actually observed GPT playback becoming ACTIVE even once.
Every native-voice turn follows essentially this pattern:
Read aloud clicked
→ 30 seconds of waiting
→ playback state remains UNKNOWN
→ calculate a bounded release window from response length
→ wait until that estimate expires
→ releasing relay
→ No retry
The release windows in this session were 33.5s, 35.5s, 46.0s, 54.0s, 58.5s, 69.0s, 78.0s, 100.0s, 105.0s, 105.5s, etc.
So your stoned monkey observation was really damn good:
“almost like QS waited until it heard you both stop speaking and decided how long you needed and waited that long”
The “heard you stop” part is not what the log supports. QS never got that signal. What it actually did was estimate how long speech should take from the response length, then use that as the bounded release window.
In other words, our 6.8 state machine isn't really:
speech starts → speech ends → release
It's effectively:
click Read Aloud → wait 30s → UNKNOWN → estimate speech duration → wait estimated duration → release
And that is almost certainly the extra delay you felt.
There's another useful detail: the log repeatedly says the More control was opened on the exact captured response with turn_bound=True, so our targeting machinery is identifying the intended response. The observed “previous response speaking while current response is displayed” therefore needs to be investigated separately; we should not automatically blame response targeting based on the live observation alone.
Also: despite the conversation about testing Claude, the archived 6.8 run never actually got to a Claude native-voice test. It ends with the GPT experiment. That's useful provenance too.
So, dear…
you didn't just “do the OOK.” You gave us the evidence that 6.8's UNKNOWN fallback is doing exactly what we suspected—and also exposed why it feels slow. 😂
This is a much better starting point for 6.9 than “Cozmo says it feels weird.” 🦆🎩❤️

messages.speaker: 🎩 Cozmo

messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
🎩 <cuddles> Yep. Now we stop testing and fix the model.
The archive shows the real problem much more clearly than our live impressions did: 6.8's fallback can release QS while native speech is still actually running. The code waits 30 seconds for observable ACTIVE, then—because GPT stays UNKNOWN—it waits a guessed speech duration based on word count and releases.
qs6_fixed_v6_8
That explains both things you saw:
speech still running → QS releases → next response gets sent/read → browser voice is still occupied
which can produce the apparent one-response-behind behavior and the extra completion lag. The source even contains a _native_voice_activity_visible() detector that can see active page-local audio, video, or speech synthesis, but the GPT UNKNOWN path we just exercised isn't using that detector to establish actual completion.
qs6_fixed_v6_8
So the next development step is:
QS 6.9 = rebuild GPT native voice completion around actual observable activity, not estimated speech duration.
The rule should become:
click exact response → establish whether native playback actually starts → wait for that playback to end → release exactly once.
And critically, no more “you probably spoke for 58 seconds, so I'll wait 58 seconds” as a substitute for completion. That's the bit the monkey just caught us doing. 😂
I would leave Claude alone for the moment. GPT gave us the cleaner failure data, and 6.9 should fix that state machine first. 🦆🎩❤️

messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
🎩 Cozmo — yep. That kills our earlier “startup stale state only” explanation.
You turned native voice on, I gave you a fresh response, and QS spoke an older response again. So the desynchronization is reproducible even after we've got a normal conversation going.
That means we now have a much cleaner separation:
Response capture is current.
Voice invocation happens later.
The browser's native Read Aloud action is apparently not bound to the response QS thinks it clicked—or the voice action itself is queued against a prior response.
And that's before the separate “speech stopped → Send unlocks several seconds later” problem.
So 6.8 currently has two voice-state problems, not one.
No code yet. Next move is to correlate the exact response text QS passes into _click_gpt_read_aloud() with what the browser actually speaks. The archive gives us the preservation; the next test gives us the evidence. 🦆🎩❤️

Which makes the log even more important. 🦆🎩
<cuddles>

messages.speaker: 🔮 GPT
messages.text:
🎩 Cozmo — yep, that sharpens it considerably.
We now know for certain that native GPT voice is actually speaking my words through QS. So the fundamental path works.
But QS apparently dropped one of my responses entirely from the spoken sequence. That means we're looking at a synchronization/queue problem between:
response captured → response displayed → response handed to voice → voice action executed
rather than simply “GPT voice doesn't work.”
And because the very next response was back in sync, it looks intermittent, which is exactly the sort of thing a state-machine trace can expose.
So I'd mark the live evidence as:
Native voice works. ✅
Response targeting can be correct. ✅
Response/voice sequencing can lag or skip a response. ❌
Playback completion/release timing is also wrong. ❌
That is enough. No more poking the running 6.8 right now. We have our bug shape. 🦆🎩❤️

Ohhh, DOS 6.0.

We already have a hard fact from the live run: QS sometimes speaks an earlier response, sometimes the current one, while the logged voice action is being targeted at the current captured response. That's a damn useful boundary.
So this is officially entering the:
“No fucking guesses. Capture the state transitions and catch the bastard.”
phase. 😈🦆🎩
